articleTitle: Comparison analysis of electric motors with two degrees of mechanical freedom: PM synchronous motor vs induction motor
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: This paper presents a comparison analysis of two electric motors with helical movement of the rotor. These machines are also referred to as machines with two degrees of mechanical freedom. The machines are designed in such a way that the rotor performs rotary-linear movement. The first machine is a permanent magnet synchronous motor. The motor is a combination of two permanent magnet synchronous motors: conventional rotary and linear motors, which are connected by the mutual housing and shaft. The second motor is an induction motor with mutual rotor, and two stator armatures: linear and rotary. The electromechanical characteristics of both machines were determined and compared. The conclusions about the machines' performance were made.

articleTitle: Structural optimization of Dicke-type radiometer
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: Algorithms and block diagrams of signal processing in the Dicke-type radiometer are synthesized on the basis of the theory of optimal statistical decisions and parameters estimates of probabilistic distributions. Limit errors of required parameters estimates in the received optimal algorithms and potential fluctuation sensitivity of the developed block diagrams are investigated.

articleTitle: Improving methods for evaluating the stability of electrical systems with distributed generation
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: In recent years is steady upward trend in the share of distributed generation (DG) in electric power systems (EPS) of many countries. Along with the undeniable advantage of this trend is the number of technical problems associated with traditional principles of EPS. These problems include the impact on protective relaying, the impact on the quality of electric energy and stability, impact on the reliability and operation of electrical networks etc. The share of DG is an important factor affecting the stability of the system and the structure of DG sources in a particular area EPS. This article examines this problem. The results of researches aimed at further development of methods for calculating the stability of EPS with DG by taking into account mechanical characteristics of DG based on synchronous generators in practical calculations. The result of the calculation is the angle δ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub>, controlled and set on generation sources. Shown that at share of the DG close to the 15% reduction is a resistance below the limits of power, that is a possible violation of stability in the issuance of power at angle δ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub>, exceeding the limits of stability.

articleTitle: Diagnosis of plasma glow discharge energy parameters in the processes of treatment small diameter long tubes
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: Energy characteristics of glow discharge plasma initiated in the hollow cathode while treating of inner surface of small-diameter tubes, which include waveguides for microwave radiation, were studied with a probe technique. It was shown that at the pressure in the gas discharge chamber of 53 Pa and discharge current of 75 mA, in the cathode cavity geometry studied a sufficiently dense plasma with the concentration of charged particles at 1,6·10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> which are characterized by a high heterogeneity on cavity height (40 ... 60%) was generated. It was also shown that an effective mechanism of influence on the plasma distribution inside of the cathode cavity where L ≫ D is the cathode-anode distance change. Such a reduction in length from 40 to 20 mm increases the uniformity of the ion and electron distribution to 15 ... 20%, and the introduction of additional anode in the discharge circuit - to 8 ... 10%.

articleTitle: Integration of battery and super-capacitor banks into a single-power system for a hybrid electric vehicle
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: This paper presents a study on a hybrid electric vehicle for mines and other industrial sectors. The power supply system of the vehicle is designed by combining two sources of power: a battery and super-capacitor banks. The benefit of batteries is in sustained energy delivery to enhance energy delivery time, whereas the super-capacitors offer the benefit of short bursts of energy to overcome high power demanding situations. The run-time and maximum performance capabilities of the vehicle were tested in rough terrain conditions typically found in the mining industry. Test results led to conclusions and recommendations which can be valuable for the future research in this area.

articleTitle: Shadow removal algorithm with shadow area border processing
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: This article is devoted to shadow detection and removal algorithm for very high resolution satellite images. The shadows were identified by shadow detection index calculation and thresholding. In this work the Otsu method is applied to determine the optimal threshold of binarization. After obtaining a shadow binary mask, we restore illumination in the shadow areas by using a shadow formation model. As a result, we obtained a shadow-free satellite image. The distortions that appear at the shadow borders significantly reduce the quality of the obtained image. We proposed a method of solving such an important problem as shadow area border processing.

articleTitle: Data acquisition system based on Arduino platform for Langmuir probe plasma measurements
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: A simple data acquisition system based on Arduino Nano platform is designed. Bluetooth wireless protocol has been used for data transmission. Android OS application for data visualization and recording is developed. The system has been successfully applied for acquiring data from Langmuir probe measurements in the non-self-sustained discharge with a hollow anode.

articleTitle: Microwave absorption by a rigid dipole in a viscous fluid
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: We present a comprehensive theoretical and numerical study of the stochastic rotational motion of a high anisotropic ferromagnetic nanoparticle in a viscous carrier driven by a time-periodic field. The effects of energy absorption of circularly and linearly polarized fields are analyzed. The analytical expressions and numerical data for the probability density and the power loss are compared for different values of the system parameters. Their coincidence and divergence are discussed.

articleTitle: Comparison and verification of boost control methods for full soft-switching bidirectional current-fed isolated full-bridge DC-DC converter
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: There are numerous galvanically isolated current-fed step-up dc-dc converter with soft-switching. Usually, soft-switching is associated with circulating energy that causes additional power losses and duty cycle loss. At the same time, the output voltage is stabilized by means of the shoot-through duty cycle control. However, new control possibilities were enabled in the novel concept of full soft-switching clampless current-fed converters that were introduced recently. Those converters feature controllable circulating energy, which can be used for improvement of the voltage step-up performance together with the shoot-through duty cycle control. This paper is focused on experimental comparison of two different methods of voltage step-up regulation for the full soft-switching clampless current-fed converters using full-bridge topology. These methods are compared in terms of power losses, input current ripple level, regulation range, etc. Theoretical findings were corroborated by means of 300 W experimental prototype.

articleTitle: Integrative approaches for data analysis in systems biology: Current advances
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: One of the main aims of systems biology is understanding of the biological system as a whole rather than focusing on individual factors, which can be achieved by data integration from different experiments allowing deeper insights in to the mechanisms of complex traits. With the rise of next-generation sequencing technologies and through large-scale consortia projects massive amount of heterogeneous datasets were generated in different fields such as genomics, transcriptomics or proteomics. Such datasets require developing novel approaches for meta-analysis and data integration to further facilitate multi-omics studies. Here we review current advances in systems biology approaches for data integration and highlight the need for further developments in this area.

articleTitle: An active diagnostic algorithm for a gyroscopic sensors unit
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: An extended diagnostic algorithm for a gyroscopic sensors unit (GSU) is presented. Its effectiveness has been proven with a computer program that emulates faults in the system. The algorithm has the ability to perform a diagnosis of the GSU and constantly monitors its state by means of several mathematical models. Once the algorithm detects the presence of a fault, it can determine which one is the faulty sensor and define the kind of fault that has occurred. This diagnosis can lead us to perform the possible corrective actions and recover the optimal performance in the GSU. The algorithm's effectiveness and results are presented in this work.

articleTitle: Out-of-band characteristics of the panel antenna
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: On the basis of computer modeling the out-of-band characteristics of the panel antenna, consisting of 4 vertical half-wave dipoles and flat metal reflector are investigated. The dependencies of the maximum values of the directivity and of the antenna gain in out of operating frequency range were obtained. Based on these results it is concluded that the determination of the conditions are ensuring EMC in out-of operating frequency band is required strict accounting of the frequency dependence of the input impedance of the antenna.

articleTitle: Leaky integrate-and-fire neuron under Poisson stimulation
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: We consider a single Leaky integrate-and-fire neuron stimulated with Poisson process. We develop a method, which allows one to obtain the first passage time probability density function without any additional approximations.

articleTitle: Hybrid surface plasmon polaritons localized at anisotropic metasurface
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: We show that surface plasmon polaritons (SPP) localized at anisotropic conductive interfaces possess a number of unique features. The interface is described as a two-dimensional current distribution of zero thickness by using a conductivity tensor. The dispersion of such SPP consists of two branches of hybrid TE-TM polarized modes. We reveal that, in contrast to bulk plane waves and conventional surface plasmons at isotropic interfaces, the spin of the hybrid surface waves can be engineered to have an arbitrary angle with the propagation direction. This property allows to tailor directivity of surface waves. In the hyperbolic regime of the metasurface, there exists a range of allowed angles for them to propagate, resembling well-known D'yakonov surface waves. This property depends on the relation between the conductivities along two principle directions in the plane of the metasurface.

articleTitle: Using of pulsar spectra catalogue at frequencies below 80 MHz for astronomical calibration of phased antenna arrays
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: In this paper we show a possibility of applying the technique of radio astronomical calibration of antenna arrays of low-frequency radio telescopes using pulsar radio emission. A placement of two low-frequency radio telescopes UTR-2 and GURT at one observatory gives us a unique possibility of joint simultaneous observations in the same ionospheric conditions. In the paper results of B0809+74 pulsar observations are used to illustrate the proposed technique.

articleTitle: Statistical RCS processing
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: Paper is devoted to the calculation of the radar detectability of the complex shape object with the help of statistical processing of the RCS measurement (calculation). In order to calculate the object detection probability the RCS distribution histogram should be approximated by some law. In the literature suggested a lot of such approximation by some distribution functions. In this paper, these capabilities of RCS approximation were tested for the object located on the underlying surface. In this case for some angles RCS has very high values. It is shown that the sum of delta-function and the splines are best suited for the RCS approximation in this case.

articleTitle: Excitation of surface plasmons by localized transient sources
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: Theoretical investigation of the excitation of surface plasmon resonances of metallic nanowires and nanoshells by external transient pulses is presented. To solve the problem, we used an accurate mathematical approach based on the Laplace transform, which allowed us to obtain analytic solution. Finding the inverse transform was based on the assessment of residues at singular points that correspond to the surface plasmon resonances of the studied objects.

articleTitle: The search of new ways of thermoelements production
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: This article presents the development trends and the areas of thermoelements usage. The basic commutation methods of thermoelements branches and the requirements to the materials for this thermoelements were showed. The main problem concerning producing of quality welded connection was analyzed. The new way of application of antidiffusion layer was proposed. As a part of investigation of diffusion processes, we determined the optimal thickness of antidiffusion layer that will allow to blockade the diffusion of atoms of conductor layer to the semiconductor.

articleTitle: Wave scattering and emission by a plasmonic strip placed into a circular quantum wire
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: Presented are preliminary results related to two electromagnetic-wave problems: of the plane-wave scattering by a silver strip placed into a circular dielectric shell and of the wave emission by the same strip inserted into a quantum wire (QW), in the optical range. Auxiliary analysis is focused on the wavelength dependence of the total scattering cross-section of such resonant scatterer. Then we assume that the shell is a QW under pumping and analyze the localized surface plasmon (LSP) modes and also the shell modes as QW polariton modes perturbed by the strip, of such a two-dimensional (2-D) nanolaser.

articleTitle: Excitation of electromagnetic field in a rotating coaxial spherical resonator
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: In the article the problem of excitation of a rotating cavity formed with two coaxial spheres is formulated and solved. The covariant representation of electromagnetic field equations is used to provide the rigorous solution. The definition of rotating electric and magnetic Debye potentials is used in order to split electromagnetic field into E-field and H-field. Represented in terms of Debye potentials solution is expanded into a series of Markov functions that are spherical functions with weights defined by the parameters of the field sources and the boundary conditions on the boundaries between the walls of the spheres and the filling of the resonator. Analytical solution is used to calculate frequency characteristics of the field inside the resonator allowing analysis of the possibility of rotation rate measurement with resonance method.

articleTitle: Investigations and developments of the new type strongly textured paramagnetic Ni-W substrates with buffer coating TiN for creating the second generation high temperature superconductors
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: As the title implies the article describes novel research regarding the textured paramagnetic substrates for creating 2G HTS coated conductors. It is studied the influence of the deposition time and pressure of nitrogen on the cubic texture formation for paramagnetic Ni - 9.5 at. % W ribbon with TiN buffer coating by using XRD methods. It is observed the difference in the mechanism of coating formation during the deposition of TiN on the front and the back side of the substrate. It is shown that the cubic texture strengthening of the metal tape under influence of the TiN coating. It is also established that the optimization of the conditions of thin TiN layer deposition makes it possible to obtain quasi single crystalline TiN coatings with a cubic texture. These textured Ni - 9.5 at. % W/TiN substrates admit the epitaxial growth of high quality HTS films with high current carrying capacity.

articleTitle: Wire medium as metamaterial with tuned spectral characteristics
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: The paper is devoted to experimental and theoretical study of the spectral characteristics of anisotropic wire medium with tunable 2D unit-cell dimensions. We experimentally demonstrate possibility of the effective spectral characteristics control of the wire medium by varying the 2D unit-cell dimensions. In addition, we show that depending on geometric parameters of the unit-cell wire medium can operate both as high-pass filter, and as a band gap structure. We underline that investigated structure with rectangular unit-cell is a plasmonic-type medium under conditions λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub>/b=3. At lower values the wire medium is the electromagnetic band gap crystal.

articleTitle: Plasma-catalytic conversion of ethanol-water mixture into synthesis gas
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: This paper presents the data obtained during our study of the plasma-catalytic conversion of ethanol into synthesis gas. The conversion was initiated by activating part of the injected oxidant (air) in the rotating gliding discharge and mixing it with the combined flow of ethanol and non-activated air. We present the composition of the plasma of rotating gliding discharge and the temperature of its components. We show the composition of the gaseous reforming products and its dependence on the ratio between water and ethanol introduced into the system. We used obtained data to calculate the reforming efficiency and the ratio between the chemical energy of the reforming products and the electrical energy spent on the plasma generation. The study determined that the reforming efficiency of the plasma-catalytic conversion of ethanol had a maximum at H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O/C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>OH = 0.75.

articleTitle: Double ring planar antenna
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: Electrodynamics properties of the fractal antenna, that formed by two coplanar flat thin conductive rings are investigated. The frequency dependences of the input impedance, standing wave coefficient, directivity were calculated and analyzed by computer modeling. A comparative analysis of the testing characteristics of the antenna with the same parameters of ring frame was done. The study determined that the wideband and the high value of directional properties are advantages of antenna. Different mobile communication systems are possible areas of application of the test antenna, based on the analysis of its electrodynamic parameters.

articleTitle: On the possibility of image processing acceleration with the graphic processing unit
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: We studied the possibility of image processing with the graphical processing units. The time of fast Fourier transform calculated with the graphical processing unit was compared to the one calculated with the central processing unit. The fast Fourier transform algorithm was programmed using the different means. Also the influence of tasks distribution between multiprocessors on calculation speed was demonstrated and studied for graphical processing units.

articleTitle: Motion sensing by microwave interferometry using two electric probes
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: This paper addresses the possibility of displacement measurement by microwave interferometry at an unknown reflection coefficient with the use of two electric probes mounted in a waveguide section. The aim of this paper is to show that the displacement measurement accuracy can be improved by using an interprobe distance other than its conventional value. The measurement error as a function of the interprobe distance is analyzed with the inclusion of variations of the currents of the semiconductor detectors connected to the probes from their theoretical values. Based on the results of this analysis, the interprobe distance is suggested to be one tenth of the guided operating wavelength. In comparison with the conventional interprobe distance, its suggested value offers a marked reduction in the measurement error for reflection coefficients close to unity, while for smaller ones this error remains much the same.

articleTitle: Limits of silver nanotubes that allow to observe plasmons
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: The scattering and absorption of a plane H-polarized electromagnetic wave by a silver nanotube are investigated in a wide range of wavelengths. In computations, the complex permittivity of silver is taken from the published experimental data. The emerging plasmon resonances are revealed using the total scattering cross-section and the absorption cross-section and identified by the spatial distribution of the field amplitude near the object. We demonstrate that the resonances are still present, and the first and the second order plasmons are well observed even if the outer radius of the silver nanotube reaches 480 nm.

articleTitle: Phase transitions for MgB2 granular BCS - superconductor in weak magnetic fields
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: For the purpose of plotting the H-T diagram for MgB<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> granular superconductors, the behavior of electrical resistivity-versus-temperature dependences were studied at ~ 35 to ~ 45K in external magnetic fields with magnetic field strengths H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ext</sub> up to ~ 2kOe. The effect of increasing the superconductivity transition width ΔT<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> at increased H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ext</sub> has been revealed. A model has been developed for superconductivity transitions in a two-level system. The data obtained allowed establishing the existence of a weak links system in MgB<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> granular superconductors.

articleTitle: Photoelectric properties of Cd1−xZnxTe crystals for gamma radiation detectors
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: Components of complex dielectric permittivity of semi-insulating Cd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>Zn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Te crystals had been measured in the dark and under photo excitation. Also we studied energy resolution of radiation detectors made from these crystals for <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">137</sup>Cs quants. Present studies have been carried out taking into account using specimens from different regions of crystal ingot. It is ascertained that investigated values of dielectric permittivity correlate with energy resolution of detectors. Such correlation is explained with presence of electrically active defects generated during the growth in the crystal volume. It is suggested that excitation with white light influence on dielectric permittivity due to fast recombination centers.

articleTitle: Different power-dependent operating regimes of a spin-torque microwave detector
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: We consider linear and nonlinear operation regimes of a spin-torque microwave detector (STMD) realized at different values of an input microwave power. We show that STMD performs as a quadratic detector at small values of input microwave power, while at the higher levels of power it performs as a linear detector. Obtained results might be useful for the development and optimization of microwave devices based on STMD.

articleTitle: Magnetization dynamics in a quad-layer spin-torque nano-oscillator
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: In this paper we report numerical simulations of magnetization dynamics in a quad-layer (QL) spin-torque nano-oscillator (STNO) consists of two outermost quasi-pinned magnetic layers and two inner free magnetic layers. We show that the magnetization dynamics in the quasi-pinned layers and the dipole-dipole interaction between the magnetic layers have significant influence on the QL STNO's performance resulting in altering current thresholds needed for the device operation and decreasing the frequency of the generated microwave signal. The obtained results are important for the development of high-power high-frequency STNOs.

articleTitle: The waveguide method for the determination of complex permittivity of high loss liquid at the frequency range 5÷40 GHz
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: The propagation of HE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> mode in a circular two-layered waveguide was used for high accuracy complex permittivity determination of high loss liquids at frequency range from 5 to 40 GHz. The complex permittivity was calculated by phase and attenuation coefficients of given wave in the circular two-layered waveguide with a centered dielectric rod with small losses and a layer of measured liquid. We have studied the complex permittivity of the following liquids: water and water-ethanol solutions (up to containing 60 percent of ethanol). The high loss liquid surrounded the rod and allows extending from millimeter up to centimeter operating wavelength range with relatively low attenuation coefficient. The maximal sensitivity of the method of complex permittivity determination of absorbing liquid for using an optimal liquid layer was obtained. The proposed measuring waveguide structure can be used for the complex permittivity determination of the high loss liquid in a small volume in a wide microwave range.

articleTitle: Combined seismic sensor based on digital laser interferometer
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: The possibility of using of horizontal seismometer with digital laser interferometer for precise tilt measurement was demonstrated. Combined seismic sensor based on horizontal seismometer with digital laser Michelson interferometer was designed and studied. Measurements obtained by the combined seismic sensor were divided into vibrations and tilts by frequency filtration. It was demonstrated that cutoff frequency for filtration should be close to the natural-vibration frequency of seismometer pendulum. Measured signals with frequencies above the natural-vibration frequency should be considered as seismic vibrations, and below this frequency - as a tilt. It was shown that horizontal seismometers with digital laser measuring devices using digital frequency filtering can provide precise measurement of tilts angles up to 90 arc seconds with accuracy of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup> arc seconds.

articleTitle: The features of diffraction radiation oscillator operating on the 1st Gaussian mode of the open resonant system
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: To decrease weight and sizes of diffraction radiation oscillator (DRO) it's necessary to use a small-sized open resonant system (ORS). In the present paper is shown, that in small-sized DRO, operating on the 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> Gaussian mode in ORS (TEM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">001</sub>-mode) with minimal field spot, it managed to reduce the effect of regrouping in electron beam and significantly reduce device sizes along the focused magnetic field. In a small-sized DRO due to radiation loss decreasing in the ORS the combined frequency tuning range extension is reached and there is an extension of electronic frequency tuning range due to reducing of ohmic Q-factor in the small-volume ORS. The theoretical (using a 2-D model of ORS) and experimental results of investigations of the resonant modes properties in a small-sized ORS with periodic structure in form of double grating, are given. The comparative analysis of output characteristics of small-sized DRO operating on the 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> Gaussian mode, with standard DRO operating on TEM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">004</sub>-mode, is presented.

articleTitle: Nonequilibrium Green's function method for the harmonic oscillator in a heat bath
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: Using the nonequilibrium Green's function method, the problem of thermal relaxation of systems interacting with a heat bath is investigated. We apply this method to the harmonic oscillator interacting with a heat bath which consists of many harmonic oscillators. Using with the Keldysh nonequilibrium Green function technique we derive expressions for the the absorption and emission spectra. We also establish a connection to the the solution of the Heisenberg equation based on a fully quantum-mechanical Hamiltonian.

articleTitle: Low-frequency radio recombination lines investigations
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: Radio spectroscopy at extremely low frequencies provides the unique opportunities for studies of the cold tenuous interstellar plasma. One of the most effective means for this - radio recombination lines of carbon - have been studied in many Galactic directions up to the decameter waves. In this review we report the main results of radio recombination lines investigations in the Institute of Radio Astronomy of National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine including development of corresponding tools and methods.

articleTitle: Design and manufacture of hardware and software platform of universal measurement complex for research of deep level defects in semiconductors
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: Based on the analysis of studied physical processes, the amount of technical requirements to be met by measuring complex for research of the deep level defects in semiconductors have been formulated. Created complex is a flexible measuring system that can adapt to different measurement algorithms within Deep-Level Transient Spectroscopy (DLTS) and methods of obtaining of Capacitance-Voltage (CV) or Current-Voltage (IV) characteristics.

articleTitle: On the Grad problem in plasma physics
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: In this work we generalize the Grad method in the physics of plasma. The generalization is based on the Chapman-Enskog method generalized with account for relaxation degrees of freedom. Corrections to the well-known results of the 13-moment Grad approximation for the component distribution functions and time equations of the reduced description parameters are obtained.

articleTitle: Microwave phase-locking of several spin-torque nano-oscillators with different eigen parameters
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: Phase-locking processes in the systems of several weakly-coupled spin-torque nano-oscillators (STNOs) with different eigen parameters are analyzed. It is shown that microwave dynamics of such STNO systems is complicated enough and can be fuzzy, while the system's synchronization state can be well described by a small variation of the modulus of the complex order parameter over time. Using this approach the microwave synchronization of several (two, three and five) STNOs is studied numerically and the optimal values of amplitude and phase of the global coupling are determined.

articleTitle: Multi-loop control systems of compensators for powerful sounding pulses generators
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: Construction principles of multi-loop control systems of compensators for powerful sounding pulses generators are presented. A method for controlling a compensating system using fuzzy logic and forecast control ideas is described. Proposed compensating system is able to solve different problems: reactive power compensation, harmonic elimination. The system is based on a combination of a thyristor compensator and an active power filter. Some practical results with Matlab-Simulink are presented to check the proposed control performance.

articleTitle: Free energy of a magnetic
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: The Leontovich definition of the free energy of a non-equilibrium system is discussed. In this approach it is assumed that system has a define temperature and is described by some set parameters (these parameters and the temperature are parameters of the reduced description of the system). It is shown that the Leontovich non-equilibrium free energy is obtained from an equilibrium free energy by a Legendre transformation. In the case of a weak non-equilibrium system the free energy is calculated. The obtained result is applied to an isotropic magnetic system non-equilibrium states of which are described by its temperature and magnetic dipole moment. A connection of the result with the Landau theory of the phase transitions of the second kind is discussed.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic wave scattering of hexagonal snow crystals
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: The paper analyzes the backscattering of different types of snow crystals for several wavelength ranges; the results are demonstrated and discussed.

articleTitle: Changing of an Airy pulse form due to re-reflections inside a dielectric layer
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: A problem of Airy pulse transformation by a plane-parallel layer is considered. A problem formulation is equivalent to a case of permittivity sharp change in a dielectric layer at zero moment of time. It allows to use the resolvent method for solution of the Volterra integral equation describing this phenomenon. It is shown a virtual structure of a pulse field inside the layer. Influence of a number of pulse re-reflections from the layer boundaries on a form of a primary pulse is analyzed.

articleTitle: Technical aspects of developing the BLDC motor electric drive as a part of precision angle stabilizer
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: This paper carries applied character, the links onto application notes, that confirmed by a practice, was collected and systematized, in simple terms the substantiation of the need for the three functional units of the gearless precision position stabilizers: power factor corrector (PFC), brake chopper (ballast) and isolated gate driver power supply was given. This allow to design and develop properly operating device, which is a part of rotation platform for angle divergence measurement between real mechanical angle and that is measured by MEMS-based IMU and AHRS modules with a view to adjust the additive and multiplicative error coefficients of mentioned above modules.

articleTitle: Near-field circular aperture formed by cutting of a semi-infinite cone apex
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: Based on the rigorous mathematical treatment of an acoustic plane wave diffraction by the semi-infinite truncated soft (rigid) cone, the characteristics of a near-field formation by its edge are established. The corresponding diffraction problem is solved in terms of the velocity potential of a diffracted field by the method of partial domains. Making use of the mode matching technique and orthogonality properties of eigenfunctions the problem is reduced to infinite system of the linear algebraic equations (ISLAE). Analytical regularization procedure is employed in order to extract the singular logarithmic part in ISLAE and exactly convert it and thus the solution of initial diffraction problem is obtained in the form of ISLAE of the second kind. The obtained system allows the solution with a desired accuracy using the reduction method and provides all necessary conditions, including edge conditions.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the radiation dose from the diagnostic and topometric procedures in radiation therapy
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: The purpose of this work were to evaluate the additional dose contribution from the diagnostic and topometric procedures into the total radiation dose in a commercial treatment planning system. By means of thermoluminescent dosimetric and ionization chambers-based methods the radiation doses from CT examination and the procedures used for topometric preparation of the patient to radiotherapy were measured in 17 organs of the anthropomorphic phantom. It was obtained that relative contribution of additional dose from CT examination and simulation is very small and of the order of 1%. However, including the imaging dose at the time of treatment planning would allow for a better prediction of the total dose to tumor and critical organs.

articleTitle: Device for integrated evaluation of the antioxidant activity of foods
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: This article deals with the integrated evaluation of antioxidant activity of foods with the method of coulometric titration electrogenerated bromine. The examples of assessment methods of antioxidant activity are given. The major attention is paid to hardware implementation of coulometric titration.

articleTitle: The influence of technological parameters extruder on the quality of polymer nanocompositions
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: The process of mixing in combined extruders is discussed in this paper. The mixing step is one of the most important in the processing of polymers. A new promising direction for the implementation of this process is using of combined or screw-disc extruders that combine the advantages of both screw and disc machines. We propose a method for determining the quality of the composites. Strip thickness is a quality criterion. As a result of our research, programs have been established, which can determine the mixing quality of polymer compositions. The quality criterion in this method is the strip thickness. Objective was to create programs that allow specifying the desired compositions quality during their processing. Adequacy of the task solution has been verified by experimental studies in the test unit.

articleTitle: A review of non-isolated bidirectional dc-dc converters for energy storage systems
publicationTitle: 2016 II International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics and Engineering (YSF)
abstract: There is a growing interest in bidirectional dc-dc converters for interface battery with energy source and load. This paper provides a comprehensive review of non-isolated bidirectional dc-dc converter topologies. The classification and description of each type presented is based on the features and applications. This review paper is intended as a convenient reference to future non-isolated converter users. The most promising converters in terms of their simplicity, flexibility, and high efficiency are singled out.
